prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: The depth map shows a top-down egocentric view where the camera wearer is seated facing forward and looking down at a wooden desk about 0.4–0.6 metres below their head, with their chest (0.2–0.3 metres) and lap (0.4–0.5 metres) in the lower foreground. On the desk within arm's reach (0.4–0.5 metres away), an open spiral notebook on the right partially occludes an open textbook underneath it on the left, while the wearer's left hand rests on the lower edge of the notebook and their right hand holds a pen about 0.1 metres to the right of the left hand. In frame 1, another person's hand and blue-clothed leg appear on the far left about 0.5–0.6 metres from the camera and 0.2 metres left of the desk before retreating out of view by frame 2, while the wearer's hands and torso remain stationary across all five frames. Compared to RGB alone, the depth map clearly separates the vertical layering of the raised right hand and pen above the flat notebook surface and the drop-off from the desk edge to the wearer's lap and floor (~0.8–1.0 metres). However, the map is unreliable at the top-left wooden cabinet edge, which is rendered bright white as if closer than the wearer's head, and it flattens the spiral binding and overlapping book boundary into nearly identical depth values.
descriptions.segmentation: The segmentation map isolates the foreground objects within the camera wearer's reach (0.3–0.6 metres away) from the unlabelled desk and floor background, showing the wearer's body and arms extending from the bottom edge toward the angled spiral notebook (labelled 'book') on the upper right and the open textbook underneath it on the upper left. Both books lie directly in front of and below the forward-facing wearer within 0.1–0.2 metres of each other, with the upper spiral notebook and the wearer's hands partially occluding the lower textbook and the pen. Across the five frames, the left neighbour's hand (labelled 'person' at ~0.5 metres on the far left in frame 1) retreats out of frame after frame 1 while the wearer's hands, torso, and the books remain static. While segmentation provides sharp pixel boundaries around the angled spiral notebook, the pen shaft, and the overlapping fingers that blend visually with the lined paper in RGB, it is highly unreliable in class stability and completeness. Specifically, the underlying textbook drops out entirely in frames 2 and 5, the wearer's body splits into multiple 'person' masks that bleed into the neighbour's leg on the lower left, the top-left cabinet is mislabelled 'book' in frame 1, and a false 'cup' mask appears on the far right edge in frame 5.
descriptions.pose: The pose map tracks the fine articulation of the camera wearer's left hand resting on the lower edge of the notebook about 0.45 metres below the head and slightly left of centre, with the fingers angled upward and to the right across all five frames. Because only the wearer's lower torso and arms are in the field of view and the neighbour on the left is mostly out of frame, no heads or gaze directions are visible, though the arm orientation confirms the wearer faces forward toward the desk with both hands within immediate reach (0.4–0.5 metres) and about 0.1 metres apart. Across frames 1 to 5, the magenta left-hand skeleton remains nearly stationary on the notebook edge, reflecting minimal movement. The map reveals precise finger joint positions for the left hand that are harder to isolate against the patterned clothing and page edges in RGB, but it is very unreliable elsewhere in the scene. It completely misses the wearer's right hand holding the pen in all five frames, misses the second person's hand on the left in frame 1, and hallucinates a distorted yellow body and face skeleton over the wearer's forearms and lap in frame 3.
